speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing progressive difficulty walking, urinary incontinence, and speech problems. To begin my assessment, have these symptoms been present for months or years, and did they start on one side of your body before affecting the other?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. Additionally, there is a history of urinary incontinence for 1 year and recent onset of speech slurring making communication challenging.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of incontinence, walking difficulty, and recent speech slurring, have you noticed any specific areas of weakness, numbness, or loss of reflexes in your legs? Also, is there any history of a spinal cord injury, tumor, or prior back surgery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple System Atrophy (Shy-Drager Syndrome)

The combination of progressive gait disturbance, urinary incontinence, and speech difficulties, now confirmed by your report of rigidity, tremor, and orthostatic hypotension, strongly points to an atypical parkinsonian syndrome with autonomic failure. I will order a Head MRI to rule out other structural causes and check autonomic function tests.
